subject: SSQ: Sensitive data routing, KMS scope, and egress controls
messages:
From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@healthco.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: security@healthco.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security questionnaire: routing of sensitive fields + KMS scope

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking our SSQ. A couple of clarifying items came up during our review and we wanted to get them in a single thread so the rest of our security team has the context. High level asks:

1) For PII fields (names, medical identifiers) — are they ever routed to third-party subprocessors for telemetry or analytics? If so, what subset and under what controls?
2) KMS scope: which keys (customer-specific vs platform) are used for storing model inputs, KV caches, and audit logs? We need a mapping for DPA annex.
3) Egress rules: we need to confirm whether any model outputs containing tokens considered PII are exported to external monitoring or 3rd-party integrations (e.g., SSO audit, analytics).

Can you include a simple diagram or matrix attachment showing flow and custody? We want to include this in our DPA Annex.

Best,
Alice
Alice Bennett
Security Engineer, HealthCo

From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@healthco.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: routing of sensitive fields + KMS scope

Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Irene (privacy lead) and Marissa (platform infra) to provide the flow diagram and the KMS mapping.

We can produce: 1) a one-page dataflow PDF showing where PII may be transiently materialized, 2) a key-scope matrix that distinguishes customer-managed keys (where available) versus Redwood-managed keys for logs/telemetry, and 3) a short write-up on our egress controls and allowed integrations.

Quick note: for our hosted offering we do ingest model inputs briefly into the KV cache in RAM and persist minimal telemetry for billing/queueing; we do not send raw PII to analytics partners by default — any telemetry that leaves the cluster is pseudonymized or aggregated. Irene will confirm the exact fields and subprocessors.

Can you confirm target audience (legal vs engineering) and if you need the files in a particular cert format? We can share the files via the shared Drive link and also send via encrypted email if preferred.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Security Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@healthco.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Security questionnaire: routing of sensitive fields + KMS scope

Forwarding internal notes and draft artifacts. See attached initial artifacts (dataflow_v2.pdf and kms_scope_matrix.xlsx). Key points that will address Alice's questions:

- Subprocessors: we use three analytics subprocessors for aggregated telemetry (TelemetryCorp, LogStream, MetricsHub). None receive raw inputs containing full PII fields. We only send hashed/pseudonymized identifiers for telemetry.
- Persistent storage: model inputs are retained in object storage for a configurable retention window (default 30 days) for debugging and billing; customers can set shorter retention via the Console and request log purges under the DPA. The DPA Annex maps retention controls.
- KMS mapping:
  * Customer-managed CMKs (when enabled): used to encrypt persisted input blobs and any exported snapshots (customer chooses key scope).
  * Redwood-managed keys: used for ephemeral caches (in-transit encryption), session tokens, and platform-level audit logs. See kms_scope_matrix.xlsx for the columns: artifact, default_key_owner, recommended_config.
- Egress: by policy we only forward aggregate telemetry to subprocessors. Integrations (e.g., SSO logs) receive alerts/metadata, never raw model output containing PII. We do have an exception process for support-driven exports under customer authorization — those are logged and require a signed export request.

I'll run this against the DPA checklist and add the paragraph calls out subprocessor contract clauses (processors only get pseudonymized data; subprocessors bound by the same SCC/P2B requirements).

Irene
Irene Choi
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@healthco.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Security questionnaire: routing of sensitive fields + KMS scope

Adding a few ops specifics and the proposed control language for the DPA Annex: 

- KV cache: in-memory only, rotated per-session, not written to durable storage except when a customer-enabled persistent snapshot is requested. Access restricted to a small set of infra hosts with RBAC and audited keystore access.
- Debug snapshots: only created when customer raises a ticket and provides explicit export authorization; snapshots are stored encrypted with the customer's CMK when CMK is enabled.
- Subprocessor list and SSO: our SSO vendor receives only identity metadata (not model outputs). The analytics subprocessors receive hashed IDs and aggregated counters.

Attachments: I’ve updated the dataflow diagram to mark custody and lifetime (see dataflow_v2.pdf) and the KMS matrix has a recommended template you can paste into your Annex.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Security, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@healthco.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Security questionnaire: routing of sensitive fields + KMS scope

Thanks — this is helpful and addresses most of our blockers. A couple of follow-ups before we close the SSQ:

1) Can you confirm the default retention window in hosted is 30 days (you noted default) and that we can set 0 days for no persistence? We’ll need the exact Console path or API call to do this for our environment.
2) For the support-driven export flow, can you share the template for the signed export request we should use so legal has the record?

If you can send revised artifacts with those two clarifications (and mark where in the dataflow the retention toggle lives), we’ll sign off and include the files in our DPA annex.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our legal and infra folks next week.

Best,
Alice
Security Engineer, HealthCo
